sections.content: Spanish often describes public processes without naming an individual actor. Use se + third-person verb for general processes, and ser + past participle when the action or result is foregrounded. These structures are common in descriptions of government and public services.

items.spanish: Se publican nuevas leyes cada año.
items.english: New laws are published every year.

items.spanish: Se ofrecen servicios públicos en la ciudad.
items.english: Public services are offered in the city.

items.spanish: La ley fue aprobada por el Parlamento.
items.english: The law was approved by Parliament.

items.spanish: Se toman decisiones importantes en estas reuniones.
items.english: Important decisions are made in these meetings.

sections.content: Use se when the actor is general or unimportant; use a passive-like form when the result or action itself is the focus.
